question: Under Maryland Business Occupations and Professions Article § 17-532, a licensee's duty to present all written offers and counteroffers to and from the client in a timely manner applies:
choice_a: Only before the property goes under contract for the first time
choice_b: Even if the real estate is already subject to an existing contract of sale or lease, unless the brokerage agreement provides otherwise
choice_c: Only to offers submitted by licensed buyer's agents, not unrepresented buyers
choice_d: Only if the offer meets or exceeds the list price
explanation: Section 17-532 requires a licensee to present all written offers and counteroffers to and from the client in a timely manner even if the property is already under an existing contract of sale or lease, unless the brokerage agreement states otherwise. The statute also makes clear the licensee need not proactively solicit additional offers on property already under contract.

question: Under § 17-532, may the duty to present all written offers and counteroffers to a client in a timely manner be waived or modified by agreement between the licensee and the client?
choice_a: Yes, if the client signs a written waiver at listing
choice_b: Yes, but only for commercial transactions
choice_c: No, this statutory duty may not be waived or modified by agreement
choice_d: Yes, if the broker's policy manual permits it
explanation: Maryland law specifies that the statutory duties owed by a licensee to a client, including the duty to timely present offers and counteroffers under § 17-532, cannot be waived or modified by agreement of the parties.

question: Under Business Occupations and Professions Article § 17-322.1, which of the following is NOT considered a material fact that a licensee must disclose about property offered for sale or lease?
choice_a: That the property has a leaking roof discovered during a pre-listing inspection
choice_b: That the seller has received and rejected a higher competing offer within the last 24 hours
choice_c: That the property's zoning classification prohibits the buyer's stated intended use
choice_d: That an occupant of the property was, is, or is suspected of being infected with HIV or diagnosed with AIDS
explanation: Section 17-322.1 provides that HIV/AIDS status of an owner or occupant, and the occurrence of a homicide, suicide, accidental death, natural death, or felony on the property, are not material facts for disclosure purposes, and a licensee cannot be disciplined or held personally liable for failing to disclose them.

question: Under § 17-322.1, a licensee's failure to disclose to a buyer that a felony or a suicide previously occurred on a property being offered for sale:
choice_a: Is not grounds for disciplinary action, and the licensee cannot be held personally liable for the non-disclosure
choice_b: Is automatically a fair housing violation
choice_c: Voids the resulting contract of sale
choice_d: Is grounds for a $5,000 fine per occurrence under § 17-322(c)
explanation: Section 17-322.1(b) expressly states it is not grounds for disciplinary action, and the licensee may not be held personally liable, for failing to disclose the stigmatized-property facts listed in subsection (a), which include a homicide, suicide, accidental or natural death, or felony occurring on the property.

question: A licensed real estate salesperson provides brokerage services to a buyer client. Under § 17-322(b)(21), from whom may that salesperson accept a commission or other valuable consideration for those services?
choice_a: Any party to the transaction who agrees in writing to pay the salesperson directly
choice_b: Only the real estate broker with whom the salesperson is affiliated, except as otherwise provided in § 17-604
choice_c: The buyer's mortgage lender, as a customary referral fee
choice_d: Any licensed title company involved in the closing
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(21) makes it grounds for discipline for an associate broker or salesperson to accept a commission or other valuable consideration for brokerage services from anyone other than the real estate broker with whom that individual is affiliated, except as otherwise provided under § 17-604.

question: Under § 17-604, a Maryland real estate broker generally may NOT pay compensation, in any form, for the provision of real estate brokerage services to:
choice_a: Any associate real estate broker affiliated with the same firm
choice_b: A branch office manager designated under § 17-320
choice_c: A person who is not licensed under Title 17, subject to specified statutory exceptions
choice_d: A licensed real estate salesperson who closed the transaction
explanation: Section 17-604 prohibits a broker from paying compensation for real estate brokerage services to a person not licensed under Title 17, with limited statutory exceptions such as out-of-state licensees meeting specified requirements, certain licensed business entities, and title insurance producers acting under written authorization.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(23), a Maryland licensee is subject to discipline for paying or receiving a rebate, profit, compensation, or commission:
choice_a: Under any circumstances, because all commission rebates are per se illegal in Maryland
choice_b: Only if the rebate exceeds 50% of the total commission
choice_c: Only if the rebate is not reported to the IRS
choice_d: Only when doing so violates some other provision of Title 17
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(23) makes it grounds for discipline to pay or receive 'a rebate, profit, compensation, or commission in violation of any provision of this title' -- meaning a rebate itself is not automatically unlawful, but paying or receiving one in a manner that violates another Title 17 provision (such as the unlicensed-compensation rule in § 17-604) is a disciplinable offense.

question: Under § 17-605, a real estate broker who wants to pay a lawyer solely for referring a person as a possible party to a residential real estate transaction:
choice_a: May not pay or offer to pay that referral commission, unless the lawyer holds a real estate broker license or is otherwise entitled to the commission
choice_b: May always pay the referral fee as long as it is disclosed on the settlement sheet
choice_c: May pay the fee only if the lawyer represents the buyer at closing
choice_d: May pay the fee freely because attorneys are exempt from Title 17 licensing entirely
explanation: Section 17-605 prohibits a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson from paying or offering to pay a commission to a lawyer simply for referring a person as a possible party to a residential real estate transaction, unless the lawyer holds a real estate broker license or is otherwise entitled to the commission; the section also bars mass solicitation of lawyers offering such fees.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(17), a licensee is subject to discipline for using a listing contract, sale contract, or advertising material that includes:
choice_a: The licensee's own personal photograph
choice_b: The name of an organization or association of which the licensee is not actually a member
choice_c: A QR code linking to the listing's virtual tour
choice_d: The property's tax parcel identification number
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(17) prohibits a licensee from using a listing contract form, a sale/rent/exchange contract form, or any advertising matter that includes the name of an organization or association of which the licensee is not a member.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(18), when a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson advertises real property for sale or rent, or advertises an offer to buy real property, the advertisement must disclose:
choice_a: The exact commission percentage the licensee will earn
choice_b: The licensee's continuing education completion date
choice_c: The name of the advertiser and the fact that the advertiser is a real estate broker, associate real estate broker, or real estate salesperson
choice_d: The seller's asking price history for the past five years
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(18) makes it grounds for discipline to advertise the sale or rent of, or an offer to buy, real property while failing to disclose in the advertisement the name of the advertiser and that the advertiser is a licensed real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson.

question: A Maryland real estate salesperson advertises a listing under his own name but does not disclose the name of the real estate broker on behalf of whom he is acting. Under § 17-322(b)(20), this is:
choice_a: Permitted as long as the salesperson's license number appears somewhere in the ad
choice_b: Permitted for digital advertisements only
choice_c: Permitted if the property is a for-sale-by-owner referral
choice_d: Grounds for license discipline
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(20) makes it grounds for discipline for a licensed associate real estate broker or salesperson to advertise the sale, rent, or offer to buy real property in their own name while failing to disclose the name of the real estate broker on whose behalf they are acting.

question: Under § 17-527.2, which of the following is included within the statutory definition of an "advertisement" that must meaningfully and conspicuously include the licensee's name and affiliated business name?
choice_a: A World Wide Web and Internet posting, a for-sale sign and sign rider, and a telephone solicitation
choice_b: Only printed newspaper classified ads
choice_c: Only paid television commercials
choice_d: Only the broker's office letterhead
explanation: Section 17-527.2 broadly defines 'advertisement' to include oral, written, or printed media, correspondence, mailings, newsletters, brochures, business cards, for-sale/for-lease signs and sign riders, promotional items, automobile signage, telephone directory listings, television and radio announcements, telephone solicitations, and World Wide Web/Internet postings, all of which must meaningfully and conspicuously include the licensee's name and the full (non-logo) name of the affiliated business.

question: Under § 17-527.2, when a licensee's affiliated business name is included in an advertisement, the statute requires that the name be:
choice_a: Printed in a font at least twice the size of the property's listed price
choice_b: The full name of the business, not merely a logo used by the business
choice_c: Accompanied by the broker's home address
choice_d: Preceded by the words "Licensed in Maryland" in all capital letters
explanation: Section 17-527.2 requires that the affiliated business name appearing in an advertisement be meaningfully and conspicuously included as the full name of the business, and that a logo alone is not sufficient to satisfy this requirement.

question: A licensee runs a print ad claiming the seller is guaranteed to earn a specific resale profit within two years. Under § 17-322(b)(8), this conduct is:
choice_a: Permitted as long as the guarantee is in writing
choice_b: Permitted only for new-construction properties
choice_c: Grounds for discipline, because a licensee may not guarantee or authorize another to guarantee future profits from the resale of real property
choice_d: Permitted if the seller requested the guarantee be advertised
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(8) makes it grounds for license discipline for a licensee to guarantee, or to authorize or allow another person to guarantee, future profits from the resale of real property.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(9), a licensee who tries to influence a prospective party to a real estate sale by offering a prize or free lot, running a lottery or contest, or advertising "free appraisals" has:
choice_a: Engaged in an acceptable marketing incentive as long as it is disclosed
choice_b: Violated only federal advertising law, not Maryland law
choice_c: Committed a violation only if the prize is worth more than $500
choice_d: Committed a disciplinable solicitation practice
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(9) specifically lists offering a prize or free lot, conducting a lottery or contest, and advertising 'free appraisals' to influence a prospective party to a sale as grounds for discipline.

question: Under § 17-606, when a licensee posts an outdoor sign or other advertisement for real property that is subject to ground rent, and the sign shows the cost or capitalization of the ground rent:
choice_a: That ground rent figure may not be shown in print or lettering smaller than the size used to show the property's price
choice_b: The ground rent figure is optional and need not appear at all
choice_c: The ground rent figure must be shown in a larger font than the price
choice_d: The sign must omit the price entirely if ground rent applies
explanation: Section 17-606 prohibits posting an outdoor sign or other advertisement for real property offered for sale or exchange that shows the cost and capitalization of ground rent in print or lettering smaller than the lettering used for the property's price -- a Maryland-specific rule tied to the state's unique ground rent system.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(16), a licensee who -- whether or not acting for monetary gain -- knowingly induces a person to sell by suggesting that the racial or ethnic composition of the neighborhood is changing and that this will lower property values is engaging in:
choice_a: Permissible market analysis if backed by comparable sales data
choice_b: Prohibited blockbusting-type conduct that is grounds for license discipline
choice_c: A federal Fair Housing Act violation only, with no Maryland state-law consequence
choice_d: Conduct that is only prohibited if done in writing
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(16) makes it grounds for discipline to knowingly induce or discourage a real estate transaction by representing that the presence of persons of a particular race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin will or may cause a decline in property values, a change in neighborhood character, increased crime, or declining school quality -- classic blockbusting conduct, prohibited regardless of monetary motive.

question: Maryland's Fair Housing law, State Government Article § 20-705, prohibits discrimination in residential real estate transactions based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, marital status, and familial status, and also based on which additional characteristics not found in the federal Fair Housing Act?
choice_a: Political party affiliation and level of education
choice_b: Credit score and employment history
choice_c: Sexual orientation, gender identity, source of income, and military status
choice_d: Immigration status and primary language spoken
explanation: State Government Article § 20-705 extends Maryland's fair housing protections beyond the federal Fair Housing Act's protected classes (race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability) to also cover marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, source of income, and military status.

question: Under State Government Article § 20-701(i), "source of income" -- a category protected under Maryland's fair housing law but not under the federal Fair Housing Act -- includes lawful income derived from:
choice_a: Only wages from full-time employment
choice_b: Only Social Security retirement benefits
choice_c: Only income verified by a W-2 form
choice_d: Employment, government or private assistance programs, gifts, pensions, and property sales, among other lawful sources
explanation: State Government Article § 20-701 defines 'source of income' broadly to include lawful money received from employment, government or private assistance, gifts, pensions, or property sales, meaning a landlord or licensee generally may not refuse to rent or sell based on how a person's income is lawfully derived, including use of a housing voucher.

question: Under State Government Article § 20-701(e), Maryland's fair housing definition of "familial status" protects households that include:
choice_a: Minors domiciled with a custodial parent or guardian, pregnant women, and individuals in the process of securing legal custody of a minor
choice_b: Only married couples with biological children
choice_c: Only households with children under age 12
choice_d: Only foster families licensed by the state
explanation: State Government Article § 20-701(e) defines 'familial status' to include one or more minors domiciled with a custodial parent or other person having legal custody, a pregnant woman, and a person in the process of securing legal custody of a minor, consistent with federal familial-status protections.

question: Under State Government Article § 20-702, the stated policy purpose of Maryland's Fair Housing subtitle is to:
choice_a: Regulate only the pricing of residential leases
choice_b: Provide fair housing throughout the State to all persons regardless of the statute's listed protected characteristics, and to prohibit discriminatory housing practices in the exercise of the State's police power
choice_c: Apply exclusively to transactions involving a licensed real estate broker
choice_d: Preempt and replace the federal Fair Housing Act within Maryland
explanation: Section 20-702 declares it State policy to provide fair housing to all persons regardless of the enumerated protected characteristics and to prohibit discriminatory housing practices as an exercise of the State's police power for the protection of the people's peace, health, safety, prosperity, and general welfare; the subtitle is administered and enforced by the Commission and, as provided by law, the State courts.

question: Under Business Occupations and Professions Article § 17-322(b)(24), a licensee's criminal conviction is grounds for discipline when the conviction is for:
choice_a: Any traffic infraction, including parking tickets
choice_b: Only convictions that occurred after the license was issued
choice_c: A felony; a misdemeanor directly related to the fitness and qualification to provide real estate brokerage services; or a crime that violates a provision of Title 17
choice_d: Only convictions in a Maryland state court
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(24) lists three categories of qualifying convictions: any felony, a misdemeanor directly related to fitness and qualification for real estate brokerage services, or a crime constituting a violation of a Title 17 provision -- under any laws of the United States or of any state, not limited to Maryland.

question: Under § 17-322(c), when the Maryland Real Estate Commission imposes a monetary penalty for a violation of § 17-322(b), the maximum penalty per violation and the factors the Commission must consider include:
choice_a: A flat $500 fine regardless of circumstances
choice_b: Up to $50,000 per violation with no consideration of mitigating factors
choice_c: No monetary penalty is authorized; only license suspension or revocation is available
choice_d: Up to $5,000 per violation, considering the seriousness of the violation, harm caused, the licensee's good faith, and any history of prior violations
explanation: Section 17-322(c) authorizes the Commission to impose a penalty of up to $5,000 for each violation, considering the seriousness of the violation, the harm caused, the licensee's good faith, and any history of previous violations; penalties are paid into the State General Fund, and no fine may be imposed solely for a violation of (b)(35) (out-of-state discipline).

question: Under § 17-322(b)(35), a Maryland real estate license may be disciplined if the licensee:
choice_a: Has been disciplined under a real estate licensing law of another jurisdiction
choice_b: Has ever practiced real estate in another state
choice_c: Fails to renew a license in another state where they are not currently practicing
choice_d: Holds a reciprocal license in Virginia
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(35) makes out-of-state real estate licensing discipline a basis for Maryland discipline, though § 17-322(c) specifically exempts violations based solely on (b)(35) from the monetary penalty provisions.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(27), a real estate broker who fails to exercise reasonable and adequate supervision over the licensees affiliated with the broker, as required by § 17-320(c), is subject to:
choice_a: No consequence, because supervision duties fall solely on individual salespersons
choice_b: Discipline by the Commission, including possible denial, reprimand, suspension, or revocation of the broker's license
choice_c: Automatic revocation with no opportunity for a hearing
choice_d: Civil liability only, with no Commission jurisdiction
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(27) makes a broker's failure to exercise reasonable and adequate supervision under § 17-320(c) a disciplinable offense, subject to the Commission's normal hearing procedures under § 17-324 before any final action is taken.

question: Before the Maryland Real Estate Commission takes final disciplinary action against a licensee under § 17-322, § 17-324 generally requires the Commission to:
choice_a: Immediately revoke the license and allow appeal only after revocation takes effect
choice_b: Notify only the licensee's broker, with no notice to the licensee
choice_c: Give the licensee an opportunity for a hearing before the Commission or a hearing board, except as otherwise provided in State Government Article § 10-226
choice_d: Refer the matter directly to a Maryland circuit court for a jury trial
explanation: Section 17-324(a) requires the Commission to give the individual an opportunity for a hearing before taking final action under § 17-322, except as otherwise provided in State Government Article § 10-226, which addresses summary/emergency suspension procedures.

question: Under § 17-324(d), when a hearing notice must be sent to an associate real estate broker or real estate salesperson, the Commission must also, at least 10 days before the hearing:
choice_a: Publish the notice in a newspaper of general circulation
choice_b: Notify the licensee's E&O insurance carrier
choice_c: Post the notice on the Commission's public website only
choice_d: Send notice of the hearing by certified mail to the last known business address of the real estate broker with whom that individual is affiliated
explanation: Section 17-324(d)(2) requires that when the individual facing discipline is an associate broker or salesperson, the Commission must also give at least 10 days' notice of the hearing to the real estate broker with whom that individual is affiliated, sent by certified mail to the broker's last known business address.

question: State Government Article § 10-226(c), cross-referenced by § 17-324(a) as an exception to the normal pre-discipline hearing requirement, allows a unit such as the Real Estate Commission to summarily suspend a license without a prior hearing when:
choice_a: The unit finds that the public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action, followed promptly by written notice of the suspension, findings, and reasons, and an opportunity to be heard
choice_b: A single consumer complaint has been filed, regardless of its substance
choice_c: The licensee has missed one continuing education deadline
choice_d: The licensee requests summary suspension in lieu of a hearing
explanation: State Government Article § 10-226(c) permits a unit to summarily suspend a license before a hearing only upon a finding that public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action, and the unit must promptly provide written notice of the suspension, its findings and reasons, and an opportunity for the licensee to be heard.

question: Under State Government Article § 10-226(b), when a licensee submits a sufficient renewal application at least two weeks before the license's expiration date, the existing license:
choice_a: Expires automatically on the stated expiration date regardless of the pending renewal
choice_b: Continues in effect until the unit acts on the renewal application and the time for judicial review has passed or any stay has expired
choice_c: Is suspended pending review of the renewal application
choice_d: Converts automatically to an inactive license
explanation: Section 10-226(b) provides that a timely and sufficient renewal application (filed at least two weeks before expiration) keeps the existing license in effect until the licensing unit acts on the application and the period for judicial review passes or any stay expires.

question: A licensee associates in a real estate transaction with another licensee, knowing that licensee is violating a provision of Title 17, and the first licensee takes no action. Under § 17-322(b)(26), this is:
choice_a: Not a violation unless the first licensee directly profits from the transaction
choice_b: Only a violation if the association lasts longer than 30 days
choice_c: Grounds for discipline against the first licensee for knowingly associating with a violation
choice_d: Only a violation if reported by the other licensee's broker
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(26) makes it grounds for discipline for a licensee, with actual knowledge of a violation, to associate with another licensee in a transaction or practice that violates any provision of Title 17.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(10) and (b)(11), which of the following listing contract practices is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Accepting an exclusive right-to-sell listing with a fixed six-month term
choice_b: Accepting a listing that includes a cancellation clause requiring written notice
choice_c: Accepting a listing that specifies a flat-fee commission structure
choice_d: Accepting a listing contract with no definite automatic termination date, or a "net" listing that leaves the licensee free to sell at any higher price and keep the difference
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(10) prohibits accepting a listing contract without a definite termination date effective automatically without notice, and (b)(11) prohibits accepting a 'net' listing contract that leaves the licensee free to sell at any price above the net return promised to the seller.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(22), a licensee who receives money belonging to a client or another party in a transaction must:
choice_a: Account for or promptly remit that money, or risk discipline for failing to do so
choice_b: Hold the funds indefinitely until the transaction closes, with no accounting required
choice_c: Deposit the funds into the licensee's personal operating account
choice_d: Report the funds only if they exceed $10,000
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(22) makes it grounds for discipline to fail to account for or to remit promptly any money that comes into a licensee's possession that belongs to another party to the transaction.

question: Under § 17-322(b)(25), a licensee who engages in conduct demonstrating bad faith, incompetency, or untrustworthiness, or that constitutes dishonest, fraudulent, or improper dealings, is:
choice_a: Exempt from discipline unless a criminal conviction also results
choice_b: Subject to discipline under this catch-all standard even if the specific conduct is not separately itemized elsewhere in § 17-322(b)
choice_c: Only subject to civil liability, not administrative discipline
choice_d: Only disciplined if a written consumer complaint is filed within 10 days
explanation: Section 17-322(b)(25) is a broad catch-all provision authorizing discipline for conduct demonstrating bad faith, incompetency, or untrustworthiness, or constituting dishonest, fraudulent, or improper dealings, independent of the other specifically enumerated grounds in the subsection.
